text.p: Following are reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A man was sentenced to six years in prison for kidnapping the son of a businessman. It was Estonia's first kidnapping case.
- President Lennart Meri is planning a high-level international conference on Baltic security in February-March next year.
- Norway will donate three million kroons to Estonian Railway to teach Estonian to railway staff. Two-thirds of the company's 8,000 staff are non-Estonians and most cannot speak Estonian.
- The Coastal Baltica Holding, the new owner of the Esoil fuel firm, intends to replace the management of the retail sales organisation EK.
- The An-72 aicraft, which ran off the runway on Saturday, was grounded by the air safety service. The aircraft will leave for a detailed checkup at the manufacturer's plant in Ukraine.
- Tartu students are protesting against the government plan to cut student subsidies for public transport.
